text: Name a famous AI or ML researcher
note: Surname is enough. Pioneers, deep learning, RL, NLP, vision, theory, robotics, safety and AI lab leaders all count

answers.q: Ran away from home at 15, co-invented the artificial neuron with McCulloch in 1943, never took a degree.
DeepMind co-founder, former chess prodigy and game designer, 2024 chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold.
Built ImageNet when most thought datasets were boring. Then co-founded World Labs.
Invented GANs in 2014, reportedly after an argument at a Montreal bar.
TD learning, the RL textbook, The Bitter Lesson, and a 2024 Turing Award with Barto.
Coined 'artificial intelligence' for the 1956 Dartmouth proposal and invented Lisp.
Co-founded MIT's AI Lab. His Perceptrons book is blamed for chilling neural nets.
Information theory, a juggling machine, a maze-solving mouse, and Dartmouth co-organizer.
Built the Mark I Perceptron in 1958. Died in a boating accident in 1971, before the revival.
Hopfield networks, 1982. Shared the 2024 physics Nobel with Hinton.
Bayesian networks, do-calculus, The Book of Why. Turing Award 2011.
VC dimension and SVMs, with Chervonenkis. Famously, 'all your Bayes are belong to us' was not his line.
Google's chief scientist. Compilers don't warn him; he warns compilers.
ResNet, Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, MAE. The most-cited paper of the century, by some counts.
First author of 'Attention Is All You Need'.
word2vec, 2013. Also showed that king − man + woman ≈ queen.
OpenAI CEO. Fired and rehired within five days in November 2023.
Left OpenAI to co-found Anthropic in 2021. Wrote 'Machines of Loving Grace'.
Led AlphaGo, AlphaZero and the RL lectures everyone watches.
LSTM co-inventor. Also co-invented, he would like you to know, most of the rest.
AlexNet co-author, seq2seq, OpenAI co-founder, then Safe Superintelligence. Feels the AGI.
Backprop popularizer, Boltzmann machine co-inventor, 2024 physics Nobel. Left Google in 2023 to warn about AI.
Convnets in 1989, cheques in the '90s, Meta's chief AI scientist, and a very active poster.
The most-cited computer scientist alive, by most counts. Turing Award 2018.
Coursera co-founder, Google Brain co-founder, Baidu's chief scientist. Taught millions gradient descent.
Coined 'Software 2.0' and 'vibe coding'. Ran Tesla Autopilot's vision team. Now teaches via YouTube.
Asked 'Can machines think?' in 1950, then swapped it for a party game.
